newsitem.title: USA: Fire at Tosco Corp U.S refinery kills worker.
newsitem.headline: Fire at Tosco Corp U.S refinery kills worker.

text.p: One worker was killed and 25 injured in an explosion and fire at a hydrocracker unit at Tosco Corp's Avon oil refinery in northern California on Tuesday night, a company spokesman said.

A loud explosion rocked the refinery near Martinez, 25 miles (40 kms) northeast of San Francisco, alarming local residents and sending flames and black smoke shooting high into the air. Nine ambulances rushed to the refinery, emergency officials said.

Tosco spokesman Jim Simmons said the fire was at a hydrocracker unit which makes gasoline. The fire was still burning five hours after it broke out, but it had been brought under control and was expected to burn itself out, Simmons said.
A refinery worker was killed in the accident, he said. The victim had not yet been positively identified. The body was in an unstable area and had not yet been recovered, he said.
"We are devastated. It's an enormous shock," Simmons said.

Twenty-five refinery employees and contractors were injured, he said. Twelve of them were taken to local hospitals and the rest treated at the refinery clinic for mostly minor injuries such as twisted knees or cuts, he said.
The blaze was restricted to the hydrocracker, Simmons said.
The cause of the explosion and fire was unknown and it was too soon to estimate damage, he said.

He said some units at the refinery were already down for maintenance before the fire. Other units not affected by the fire were still operating, he said. The refinery has a capacity of 150,000 barrels per day.
